questions: Q1: Does the CLI check command correctly implement POST trigger + GET polling with specified intervals?
Q2: Does the CLI follow the existing goals/ command group pattern?
Q3: Are the API paths and communication correct?

answers.answer: Yes. check.ts implements POST to /playbook/rules/${ruleId}/check with basePath: '/api', then polls GET /playbook/rules/${ruleId}/checks/${check.id} every 5 seconds (POLL_INTERVAL_MS=5000) for up to 120 iterations (MAX_POLLS=120, 10 minutes). Terminal states PASS, FAIL, ERROR correctly detected. Handles immediately-terminal checks (e.g., GENERAL org ERROR). --json flag for machine-readable output. Exit code 0 for PASS, 1 otherwise.
evidence: check.ts L60-63: POST trigger with basePath: '/api'
check.ts L80-94: GET poll loop with sleep + terminal check

answers.answer: Yes. src/playbook/index.ts mirrors src/goals/index.ts exactly: switch-based subcommand dispatch, help text display, parseApiError error handling (imported from goals/utils.ts), isHelpRequested checks for both router and subcommands. The main dispatcher (src/index.ts) registers the playbook case using the same configOrHelp pattern as goals.

playbook/index.ts L5: imports parseApiError from goals/utils.js
index.ts L133-136: playbook case matches goals case pattern

answers.answer: Yes. All hxFetch calls use basePath: '/api' which maps to the server's /api router prefix. Paths match the server routes exactly: POST /playbook/rules/${ruleId}/check, GET /playbook/rules/${ruleId}/checks/${checkId}, GET /playbook/rules/${ruleId}/checks. hxFetch handles auth (API key header) and retries automatically.
